## The floating timer, the update reminder, and the notification — all had the same problem

Each of these was shipped, each had a switch, and none of them ever appeared. The
cause was the same in three different places: **something failed and the failure
was swallowed.**

- **Floating timer (Windows)** now opens. The window was there all along; the app
  was not allowed to show it, because the permission list was missing the window
  calls. Fixed, and the Settings switch now says why if it ever can't.
- **Update reminder** now appears on every launch, not only when the last check
  was six hours old. The last "update available" answer is remembered, so the
  strip is already on screen while the app asks again. And a failed install no
  longer hides the reminder — that is what made it vanish for a version that
  never actually installed.
- **Android notification** now asks for permission when you open the app, instead
  of only when a session starts (where the first notification was lost behind
  the dialog). New: **Settings → Notifications** on mobile shows whether it is
  allowed, with a button to enable it.

## What to check

1. **Windows**: Settings → Floating timer → on. A small stopwatch window appears;
   drag it anywhere, pin it on top, expand to the app.
2. **Android**: Settings → Notifications → Enable. Start a session: the live
   timer appears in the shade with Pause and Stop.
3. **Both**: reopen the app — if a newer release exists, the strip at the top of
   every screen says so.
